title: Microsoft Purview: DLP for file and text traffic through Entra Global Secure Access Internet Access
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says Endpoint DLP cannot protect sensitive content shared with unapproved cloud apps, although Microsoft documents that protection. The Entra configuration path also skips opening a new rule before selecting its action; the roadmap facts, licence combinations and reported pay-as-you-go disagreement are supported.

claims.quote: Global Secure Access forwards matching upload traffic to Microsoft Purview for content inspection. Purview evaluates the content against your DLP policy and returns a decision based on your DLP rule action. Global Secure Access then enforces the result.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Traffic not mapped to an Entra user identity is not sent to Purview for inspection.
claims.quote: Scan with Purview only applies to traffic associated with an Entra user identity. Traffic that cannot be mapped to an Entra user identity is not sent to Purview for inspection.

claims.claim: Network data security policies do not apply to B2B guest users.
claims.quote: Purview network data security policies don't apply to B2B guest users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Conditional Access policy scopes application of the security profile to selected users and groups.
claims.quote: To enforce the Global Secure Access security profile, create a Conditional Access policy with the following configuration: ... Select the users and groups to apply the policy to.

claims.claim: The Global Secure Access content policy page lists a 3 MB Scan with Purview maximum for files and text.

claims.claim: OCR is not yet supported for traffic sent to Purview.
claims.quote: OCR is not yet supported for traffic sent to Purview.

claims.claim: WebSocket traffic bypasses file-type filtering.
claims.quote: WebSocket traffic bypasses file-type filtering in Content policy rules.

claims.claim: Text content types are still evaluated within WebSockets.
claims.quote: Text content type is still evaluated within web sockets.

claims.claim: File detection is limited to unencoded and multipart-encoded request or response bodies.
claims.quote: File detection is limited to files transferred as request/response bodies unencoded and with multipart encoding.

claims.claim: Encoding a file in JSON or splitting it across encrypted requests can prevent inspection.
claims.quote: Certain file transfer methods may prevent inspection, such as if an application encodes a file within a JSON, or the file is broken up into multiple encrypted requests.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Traffic fails open when Purview inspection cannot complete.
claims.quote: In scenarios where Purview inspection is unable to complete, such as a payload that is too large to inspect, or an internal error, the traffic is allowed (fail-open).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout

claims.quote: Transactions that have skipped inspection can be identified in Traffic logs using PurviewStatus field.

claims.claim: Requests are subject to API rate limiting based on usage.
claims.quote: Requests are subject to API rate limiting based on usage.

claims.claim: Exceeding the API rate limits blocks traffic, failing closed.
claims.quote: When limits are exceeded, traffic is automatically blocked (fail-closed).

claims.claim: Blocking HTML or JSON text types in basic content filtering can block normal web and API traffic.
claims.quote: Web requests and responses commonly use HTML or JSON payloads, so blocking these text types can unintentionally block normal web and API traffic, including GET, POST, and PUT operations.

claims.quote: Some features used in this scenario are in preview.

claims.claim: Endpoint and Microsoft 365 DLP do not reach files and text sent from managed devices to unsanctioned apps.
claims.quote: This scenario demonstrates how to restrict unintentional sharing of sensitive information to unapproved cloud applications and services using Microsoft Purview DLP.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'This extends Purview DLP inspection to files and text routed through Global Secure Access to unmanaged cloud apps.' The cited content filtering page supports that narrower statement; do not claim Endpoint DLP cannot protect sharing to unapproved apps.

claims.fix: Include the omitted app-scope selection in both copies of the path: 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes > app categories > Choose where to enforce the policy > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers'.

claims.quote: Checklist: 'Enable the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile, check user assignments and configure a TLS inspection policy'; 'Review Purview Data loss prevention > Alerts and Activity explorer'. The table has only DLP policy and content policy rows.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Enable the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile' and the After rollout bullet beginning 'Review Purview'. Replace the At rollout content-policy bullet with 'Create a Global Secure Access content policy with a Scan with Purview rule whose activities and content types match the DLP rule's actions.' Replace its validation bullet with 'Validate each activity you rely on with a test file or text.' These remove checklist instructions for forwarding, TLS, profile linking, Conditional Access and monitoring controls that lack rows; retain the factual explanations elsewhere.
